strategic_idea: HSBC's Asian wealth metals franchise is vertically integrated but product-thin outside Hong Kong: the only scaled products are two HK book-entry items (Wayfoong Statement Gold, ~4% max spread, and the SFC-authorised HSBC Gold Token, >US$1bn traded, 2%/5% margin, vaulted in London not Hong Kong), a counter-only Malaysian gold account, HSBC China's gold-linked structured deposits (GLD/GDX and gold-miner baskets, Jan-2026) and the custodian/dealer seat on the new Hang Seng Gold ETF (3170, HK$1.3bn). There is no physical bullion sale, no gold-linked deposit in HK/SG, nothing in Singapore, Taiwan, India (HSBC also lost/never held a 2026-29 bullion-import licence) or Australia, and no published PB precious-metals brochure or metal-collateral Lombard terms. a global wealth franchise Asia is behind on the digital/paper-gold rail (no SFC-authorised token, no house paper-gold account with WSG's distribution) but can out-position HSBC where the desk has product: (1) allocated loco-London and loco-Hong Kong/Singapore physical custody for GPB/Premier-Elite-equivalent clients with delivery optionality (HSBC's token and WSG both bar delivery); (2) PM margin loans / share-backed lending against bullion, gold ETFs (2840/3170/GLD) and gold-miner equity - HSBC's Lombard shelf does not publish metal collateral; (3) gold-linked structured deposits and dual-currency-style XAU products for HK/SG affluent clients, matching what HSBC China sells but HSBC HK/SG do not; (4) OTC gold options, accumulators and zero-cost collars for UHNW; (5) a Singapore-booked gold account/physical offer where HSBC SG has nothing, timed with MAS loco-Singapore vaulting (Oct-2026). The 62% of Asia/Middle East affluent investors intending to add gold in 2026 (HSBC's own survey) is demand HSBC's non-HK entities cannot currently serve with a proprietary product.
